newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israeli shares close broadly higher.
newsitem.headline: Israeli shares close broadly higher.

text.p: Israeli shares closed higher across the board on Wednesday as investors gained confidence after prosecutors vindicated Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu of a corruption scandal, traders said.

The benchmark Mishtanim index of the top 100 shares rose 1.20 percent, or 2.96 points, to 250.64 on an all-share turnover of 83 million shekels against 95 million shekels on Sunday, the last day of trading before the Jewish holiday of Passover.
The Maof 25 blue chip index closed 1.51 percent higher at 261.50.

Prosecutors on Sunday rejected a police recommendation that they should charge Netanyahu with fraud and breach of trust in the short-lived appointment in January of Roni Bar-On as attorney-general, allegedly as part of a shady deal with a political ally on trial for corruption.
Prosecutors said they found insufficient evidence to issue the first indictment against an Israeli prime minister.

"The market continues to show strength today and despite the fact that activity is usually low on holidays volume was relatively high with the market rising across the board," said Danni Scharia at Capital Securities.
Trading hours on the Tel Aviv Stock Exchange were reduced on Wednesday for the Passover holiday.

"On Sunday the market was very nervous because of the political scandal, but now it has gained confidence again and I believe that the positive momentum will continue. The market believes that Netanyahu's government is strong enough to continue," Scharia said.
"Investors were satisfied with the prosecution's decision and the fear that the market will suffer from the political uncertainty is gone," said Sahar Gazit at Batucha Securities and Investments.
"If it was not for Teva the Maof index would have closed today with a rise of more than two percent," Scahria added.

Teva Pharmaceutical Industries, the most active share and the main loser on the Maof, plunged 5.5 percent to 16,877 agorot on volume of 15.7 million shekel. Traders said Teva fell as it almost closed the arbitrage gap with its issue traded on Nasdaq.

Other active shares included Israel Discount Bank, which rose 2.0 percent to 344 agorot on volume of 6.8 million shekels; and Koor Industries which closed unchanged at 30,113 agorot on turnover of 4.7 million shekels.
